mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 0.5% quarter-over-quarter signals stronger household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline when GDPC1 acceleration exceeds 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals labor market tightness that raises wage growth and inflation, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline when UNRATE falls below 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -1% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline when INDPRO falls below -1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below -0.5% quarter-over-quarter signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline when GDPC1 falls below -0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% signals labor market slack that reduces wage growth and inflation, which lowers discount rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline when UNRATE exceeds 6% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month signals labor market strength that raises wage growth and inflation, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline when PAYEMS exceeds 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).
